title: Kestrel Auto Finance Portfolio Exposure Standard
content:
**Standard.** Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts are aggregated per customer over the customer's contracts whose status is active, counting them and summing their principal balances at the moment of the request. A new approval is written only when the count of the customer's active contracts plus the new one does not exceed the new tier's maximum active contracts, and the combined principal of the active contracts plus the new amount financed does not exceed the new tier's maximum aggregate exposure. The limits of the tier being approved apply, not those of the customer's older contracts. An approval refused on these grounds is not written; the customer may apply again after paying a contract down.

## Basis of the test

- **Evidence:** the system record of the customer's contracts — which of them have status active, and the principal balance of each. A customer's own account of their balances is not the basis.
- **Object:** the contracts held under the same customer as the new application.
- **Figures:** the maximum active contracts and the maximum aggregate exposure in the tier's exposure ceilings, read for the tier being approved.
- **Equality:** reaching a ceiling exactly is within it ("does not exceed").

## Decision table

| Active contracts plus the new one | Combined principal plus the new amount financed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| does not exceed the new tier's maximum | does not exceed the new tier's maximum | approval written |
| exceeds the maximum | any | approval not written |
| any | exceeds the maximum | approval not written |

## Hypothetical cases

- A customer holds one active contract with a principal balance of 18000.00 and is approved at a tier whose ceilings are 2 contracts and 50000.00. With a new amount financed of 32000.00 the totals are 2 contracts and exactly 50000.00: the approval is written.
- The same customer with a new amount financed of 32000.01 reaches 50000.01: the approval is not written. After the existing contract is paid down so that the combined principal no longer exceeds the ceiling, the customer may apply again.
- A paid-off or unwound contract is not active and is not counted.
